value.literal: Typed feature builders describe views, queries, events and behaviour. References point to declarations, not copied strings.
The intermediate representation stores those declarations and their relationships. The same structure is available to every tool.
Rules catch invalid references and unsafe data flow. Contracts exercise machine transitions against the intended result.
Scope and freshness determine rendering regions. Machine bindings determine the islands that need client JavaScript.
The server renders HTML and serializes data. The browser only hydrates the interactive islands that the plan calls for.
Change the declarations. This illustrates one query in a static shell; nested dependencies can make a region more dynamic.

aria-label.literal: Declared scope and freshness feed the compiler, which derives a render region.
Scope and freshness flow into the compiler and determine the render region.

value.literal: Public, static data can be rendered ahead of time. A view without machine bindings ships no client application JavaScript.
Public data uses the declared revalidation interval. The cached region can be regenerated by a server; this is not a GitHub Pages-only deployment.
Public cached data can be served while the server refreshes it. Cache policy follows the declaration rather than a route-level override.
Live freshness requires request-time data and the framework’s live transport. It cannot be exported as a static-only page.
User scope wins over every freshness choice. This data must never reach a shared cacheable region; it needs a server.
Hydration is a separate decision: only machine-bound nodes become islands. These controls are native HTML and use no JavaScript.
Hozu (ほぞ). A precise fit between intent and implementation.
Built with Hozu. HTML first, with room to explore.
Built for agents that change software.
Invalid programs are hard to express. Valid programs are cheap to verify.
Hozu is a web framework for coding agents. When a change looks right and still type-checks, Hozu reports what broke, where, and how to fix it.
ほぞ / A joint that fits.
What an agent gets wrong, and what Hozu says.
Each of these changes type-checks and builds. The diagnostics are the real output of hozu check on the same mistake, wrapped to fit.

features/notes/views.ts:9:14  error  HZ022
Public query notes.notesOf is keyed by user-scoped data
cause: Its result is cached in the shared public partition (revalidate), so user-derived input would reach a cacheable region.
fix: Make the query scope: 'user', or key it by data that does not come from the user
Conventional column: an illustration of the failure. Hozu column: hozu check on this mistake.

Method "sort" cannot run on a reference: references are recorded, not evaluated. For a list use ui.each(list, 'id', (item) => …); for any other computation declare a fn() and call it with the reference.

Create an app, add a feature, check your work. Node 22.18 or newer.
Use --agent agents for Codex, Cursor or Copilot; --agent claude for Claude Code.
The IR is the source of truth
Typed builders describe your app as data. The validator, compiler and runtime share one representation.
Given a state, when an event happens, expect a result. Every machine transition has a contract.
Declare who can see data and how fresh it must be. Hozu derives the render plan; only machine-bound views hydrate.
Diagnostics that lead to a fix
Each diagnostic carries a location, a cause and a suggested fix. Read it yourself or pass the JSON to your agent.
Hozu is not a separate SPA mode or a place for arbitrary effects in views. It makes behaviour explicit, and asks you to pay for that structure.
Measured, with the rough edges included.

Two tasks, each built from a spec and then changed by an agent, checked by hidden acceptance tests. Notes: accounts, per-user isolation, double submit, forms without JavaScript, HttpOnly sessions. City bikes: a Leaflet map, a Chart.js chart, GSAP animation and a Three.js globe. Every run is also re-checked after the change for regressions.
Trials 0012, 0017 and 0019: the same tasks, prompts and model; agent cost relative to Nuxt

One Nuxt change silently broke three working features; no Hozu run did. The price is extra tokens: a guide the model has not seen, and on widget-heavy apps more code to write. Two to four runs per step: small samples, not failure rates.
0018: city bikes on 0.6, with hozu browse
0016: notes on 0.5, four runs per step and a Codex run
